html:
Contrast

You might say

That gray helper text on the page strains my eyes—make it readable.

Contrast is the brightness difference between text and background—big enough to read; light gray on light gray is not.·Light gray body text on a gray background almost vanishes when you squint—that is insufficient contrast. To turn "hard to read" into a checkable requirement, tell the AI "keep body text at 4.5:1 contrast against the background," the common industry threshold. Dark mode fails here most often: black backgrounds paired with the old gray look layered but sit below the line.
Know first
Dark Mode
One sentence, two contrast levels
Light background
Organize project background, process, and results into a shareable page.
Gray on light gray: vanishes when you squint
Body 4.5:1, secondary 3:1—speak in ratiosRe-check dark mode; don't reuse the light-mode text shade.
Two thresholds that suffice

Readable text 4.5:1: Headings, body, captions, button labels—everything meant for real reading needs at least 4.5:1 against its background.

Large text and icons 3:1: Big headlines, icons, and button borders that carry no paragraph-level reading duty start at 3:1—anything lower becomes invisible.

What it is not

Contrast is not "do the colors look good"—aesthetics is a separate question; contrast only answers legibility. It covers more than text: icons, button borders, and form outlines have thresholds too. Re-check dark mode separately instead of reusing the light-mode text colors.
